NONE: › to get enjoyment from something, especially something unpleasant
（尤指從令人不愉快的事中）得到樂趣，獲得享受
› an enjoyable activity or celebration
歡慶；歡宴
› happy and smiling
興高采烈的，快活的
› old-fashioned enjoyable, energetic, and entertaining
令人愉快的，愜意的
› mainly UK bright and attractive
明亮好看的
› very
很，非常
› to encourage someone to do something by putting that person in a good mood and persuading them gently
（說好話）哄，捧，鼓勵

example: a jolly smile/manner/mood
開心的微笑／興高采烈的樣子／愉快的心情
She's a very jolly, upbeat sort of a person.
她是個非常樂觀向上的人。
a jolly occasion
令人愉快的場合
We spent a very jolly evening together, chatting and reminiscing.
我們一起聊天話舊，度過了一個愜意的晚上。
I love the bright yellow you've painted the children's room - it makes it look really jolly.
我喜歡你給孩子房間塗刷的鮮黃色——這使它看起來十分明亮悅目。
That's a jolly nice scarf you're wearing.
你戴的圍巾很漂亮。
I'll try to jolly my parents into letting me borrow the car this weekend.
我會試著哄我爸媽週末把汽車借給我。
She didn't really want to go to the party, so we had to jolly her along a little.
她並不太想參加聚會，所以我們要哄得她高興點。

NONE: › used to express approval of something that someone has said or done, or to show that you have heard or understood what someone has said
（表示贊同、已聽到或明白）很好

example: "I've left all the papers you need on your desk." "Oh, jolly good."
「我把你需要的文件都放在你桌子上了。」「噢，很好。」

NONE: › used to express admiration for what someone has said or done
（表示讚賞）做得好！太棒了！

example: "We won!" "Oh, jolly good show!"
「我們贏了！」「啊，太棒了！」

NONE: › used to describe a woman or girl of a high social class who is enthusiastic in a way that annoys most people
（上層社會女子）好交際的，過分熱情而讓人討厭的
› to make something brighter and more attractive
使更明亮悅目

example: I thought I'd jolly the room up with some colourful curtains.
我想我會用些色彩鮮艷的窗簾讓房間更明亮好看。

NONE: › used to emphasize something you are saying, especially when you are angry or annoyed
（用於生氣或煩心時加強語氣）

example: I'm going to jolly well tell her what I think of her!
我這就去告訴她我對她的看法！
"Is she ready to leave yet?" "I jolly well hope so!"
「她是不是準備要走啦？」「我倒是希望她走呢！」

I or T, usually + adv/prep: › [ I or T,  usually + adv/prep ] to (cause something or someone to) move suddenly and violently

T: › [ T ] to shock someone in order to change their behaviour or way of thinking

NONE: › to give someone a sudden shock that forces them to act
使（某人）受到震驚（而採取行動）；使（某人）從…中覺醒

example: The train stopped unexpectedly and we were jolted forwards.
火車突然停住了，我們都猛然向前晃了一下。
The truck jolted along the rough track through the field.
卡車沿著田野裡崎嶇的小路顛簸前行。
The charity used photos of starving children in an attempt to jolt the public conscience (= make people feel guilty and take action).
慈善機構用飢餓兒童的照片來觸發大眾的良知。
The news about Sam's illness jolted her into action.
山姆生病的消息使她頓然醒覺，開始採取行動。
As the plane touched the ground, there was a massive jolt and we were thrown forwards.
飛機著陸時劇烈震動，我們被猛地甩向前方。
I woke up with a jolt as I thought I heard my bedroom door being pushed open.
我好像聽到自己臥室的門被推開，猛地驚醒了。
His self-confidence took a sudden jolt with the news that he had not been selected.
他未能獲選的消息使他的自信心遭受意外打擊。
